To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
photoperiod affects food intake in Soay rams and this effect is related to the expression of neuropeptide Y in the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenocortical axis.
the photoperiod-induced change in VFI in Soay rams is associated with changes in expression of genes for appetite regulating peptides.
photoperiodic regulation of food intake involves changes in expression of genes for NPY, but does not involve changes in expression of other putative orexinergic genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying photoperiod-induced changes in appetite and bodyweight in ruminants.
understanding the molecular basis of seasonal changes in food intake in ruminants, which is of considerable economic importance.
the role of photoperiod in the regulation of appetite and reproduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
photoperiod regulates appetite through NPY and leptin receptor expression.
the photoperiod regulates the expression of the genes for NPY, AgRP and Ob-Rb in the ARC and that these genes play an important role in the photoperiodic regulation of VFI in rams.
photoperiodic effects in the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis are not mediated by changes in appetite regulating genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
photoperiod regulates VFI through NPY and Ob-Rb gene regulation.

the photoperiodic effects of NPY, agouti related protein, melanin concentrating hormone, orexin and leptins on the appetite of Soay ram is mediated by a complex interaction between the photoperiod, body weight and sexual state of the ram.
NPY and Ob-Rb are the most sensitive markers for photoperiodic regulation of food intake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
photoperiodic changes in VFI correlate with NPY mRNA levels in the ARC.
the photoperiodic effects are not due to a change in body weight, fatness or leptin levels, but rather are a direct effect of the change in photoperiod.
the photoperiodic regulation of VFI in the Soay ram is not dependent on a change in the expression of the appetite regulatory genes examined here.
